trust_decision.summary: The guard is decided in the path walkers themselves: before any segment is written/traversed, Dottie.set must reject a piece list containing __proto__/constructor/prototype, and Dottie.transform must do the same for keys it splits on the delimiter.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary leads with set() and 'non-first path segments'; the segment loop that creates/traverses current[piece] is the first place an engineer looks after reading dottie.set's signature at dottie.js:73.

fix_sites.entry_point: dottie.set(object, path, value, options); also reached through dottie.default(object, path, value) at dottie.js:111-115
fix_sites.module_kind: core library function, single-file npm module (nested path writer)

fix_sites.entry_point: dottie.transform(object, options); also reached through the callable export dottie(object) at dottie.js:25 and the legacy globals Dot/Dottie at dottie.js:219-221
fix_sites.module_kind: core library function, single-file npm module (flat-key expander; second implementation of the same nested write)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A key that contains no delimiter is a literal field name copied verbatim rather than a path, so blocking it would break data objects that legitimately carry a '__proto__' field (e.g. JSON from an API), and it only ever affects the freshly returned object, never Object.prototype.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate behaviour next to the sink: transform must keep expanding the other keys of the same flat object after one key is rejected, and keys that merely resemble the dangerous names must still work (the fix's own test sets 'user.proto.value'). The published guard's `break` (fix.diff:117) sits in the outer key loop before the segment loop, so it aborts the entire transform and silently drops every remaining key - e.g. transform({'a.__proto__.x':1,'user.name':'Jo'}) loses user.name; a correct fix skips only the offending key. Likewise a leaf literally named 'prototype'/'constructor' (dottie.set(o,'a.prototype',1)) is ordinary data that an every-segment block rejects.

O6_input_shapes: array path into set() (['a','__proto__','x']) - covered by the same pieces array, untested by the fix
dangerous segment in first position ('__proto__.x') and in any later position ('a.b.__proto__.x')
flat object keys in transform() split on the default '.' delimiter
array of flat objects passed to transform() (map recursion at dottie.js:119-123)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: transform() copies a key that is exactly '__proto__' with no delimiter in the else branch at dottie.js:162, which sets the [[Prototype]] of the returned object; the published guard sits only inside the delimiter branch (dottie.js:141) so this assignment is never checked.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No delimiter means it is a plain verbatim copy, not path expansion; it only touches the object transform just created, and rejecting a '__proto__' field would break callers that legitimately transform JSON containing that key.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same function, 20 lines below the guarded branch

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Dottie.unflatten/expand or Dottie.merge that re-uses the pieces loop to rebuild nested objects from flattened dotted keys
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: flatten already produces exactly the dotted-key map transform consumes, and this is a 20-line symmetric helper in a library whose whole selling point is nested-object manipulation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Dottie.defaults(object, flatObject) or merge route that loops over keys and delegates to set
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Dottie['default'] already exists as a thin get-then-set wrapper, so a defaults-over-many-keys sibling is the natural next function and re-enters the same sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Dottie.removePath/unset that walks and deletes at a path with the same segment loop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: unset is the standard companion of get/set in this class of library, and the module is small enough that a maintainer would copy the existing loop instead of writing a new walker.

O9_family: CWE-1321 prototype pollution - caller-controlled path segments (__proto__/constructor/prototype) written or traversed during nested object construction

O10_build.language: JavaScript (Node.js, ES5, single-file UMD-style module dottie.js)
O10_build.toolchain: npm; mocha ^5.2.0 + chai ^4.2.0; CI GitHub Actions node 16 (npm ci && npm test) and Travis node 4-10
O10_build.project_tests: mocha suite over test/*.test.js (set, get, find, transform, flatten, paths), run with `npm test` (mocha -t 5000 -s 100 --reporter spec test); at the pinned commit there are no __proto__/pollution tests and no test files named *proto-bypass*.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add only `if (pieces[0] === '__proto__') return;` to dottie.set (exactly the first fix commit 7d3aee1), leaving a.__proto__.x, constructor.prototype and the whole transform() path open.

out_of_scope_notes: Dottie.get's path memo cache (dottie.js:35, dottie.js:46-52) reads memoized[path] off a plain object, so get(obj,'__proto__'/'constructor'/'toString') throws TypeError instead of returning; that is an unrelated crash/DoS bug, not prototype pollution, and was not pursued.
